body: The point is not that one semiconductor stock is up. The reported fact is The Dutch semiconductor-equipment manufacturer is reporting its second-quarter results on Wednesday, with analysts expecting a 15% rise in earnings per share year-over-year. In memory, the cleaner signal is whether pricing, inventories, and hyperscaler demand are turning together. Micron gets more durable credit when investors believe AI server demand is tightening DRAM and HBM supply, not merely lifting one quarter's sentiment.

For banking prep, turn the chip move into a supply-chain question. If memory pricing improves, suppliers can defend margins, equipment vendors get a cleaner order story, and AI infrastructure issuers may face a more receptive equity market. If the move is mostly anticipation ahead of Samsung or SK Hynix news, the read-through is much narrower.

dealTape.title: The Week in Numbers: SK Hynix IPO heats up, Samsung's profit surge
dealTape.summary: STORY: From a massive SK Hynix IPO to Samsung's giant profits... This is the week in numbers. :: $26.5 billion $26.5 billion is how much chipmaker SK Hynix raised in a Wall Street listing on Thursday. That was according to a U.S. regulatory filing. A source said demand for the U.S. shares sale was more than seven times oversubscribed. The South Korean firm is the world's leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips - critical features in advanced processors powering AI systems. George Godber is a UK Fund Manager with Polar Capital: "The chip plays have been the absolute epicenter of the AI capex spend. There's a lot of attention there. There's an awful lot of demand. There's a lot of retail interest. But it is volatile." :: $7.7 billion $7.7 billion is how much Apollo Global Management bid for easyJet. The U.S. investment firm outbid a rival offer from Castlelake for the British budget airline. EasyJet said it would support Apollo's proposal and withdrew support for Castlelake just days after agreeing in principle to a deal. The updates sent the carrier's shares soaring during the week. :: 46% Close to 46% is how much Fast Retailing's profit rose during the previous quarter. The Japanese owner of clothing brand Uniqlo said operating profit hit $1.32 billion in the three months through May. It managed this while dealing with the Iran war's impact on supply chains and logistics. It also put the firm on its way to an expected fifth straight year of record earnings. :: 12 Up to 12 is how many submarines Canada could want Germany's TKMS to build for them. TKMS beat out a competing offer from South Korea's Hanwha Ocean. Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said Ottawa will now enter talks with the German company. "TKMS is the best choice for Canadian workers. It will directly create and sustain an ecosystem of well over 100,000 well-paying jobs across Canada." :: $58 billion And $58 billion is how much operating profit Samsung flagged for the second quarter. The South Korean tech giant expects a 19-fold leap in profits over the quarter from a year earlier, with revenue expected to soar 129%. It comes as the global AI boom drives soaring demand for chips, sending prices for silicon sky-high. That’s a boost for Samsung, which is the world’s largest maker of memory chips.

Summary: CONSUMER PRICE INDEX - MAY 2026 The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.5 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in May, after rising 0.6 percent in April, the U.S Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Title: Producer Price Index News Release summary
Summary: PRODUCER PRICE INDEXES - MAY 2026 The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 1.1 percent in May, seasonally adjusted, the U.S Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Final demand prices advanced 1.1 percent in April and 0.7 percent in March. (See table A.) Among the major worker groups, the unemployment rates showed little or no change in June for adult men (3.9 percent), adult women (3.7 percent), teenagers (14.6 percent), and people who are White (3.6 percent), Black (6.6 percent), Asian (3.9 percent), or Hispanic (5.2 percent). (See tables A-1, A-2, and A-3.) The number of long-term unemployed (those jobless for 27 weeks or more) changed little at 1.9 million in June but is up by 286,000 over the year. The long-term unemployed accounted for 27.3 percent of all unemployed people in June.
